zero_case_final_attachment_step.argument: Use lem-cw-homotopy-equivalence-inclusions-are-strong-deformation-retracts, second clause, on a single interval attached to S2 at its two endpoints. Move one endpoint along a supplied meridian path until both endpoints coincide. The resulting attachment is S2∨S1, and the lemma gives the homotopy equivalence relative to S2. Thus the zero-crossing cubical spine already constructed in supplement1 has the claimed S1∨S2 homotopy type, without a new unproved attachment-invariance premise.

upper_handlebody_local_model.argument: For a straight diameter arc in a unit 3-ball and cylindrical tube of radius epsilon, its compact exterior is explicitly S1×D where D={(r,z):r>=epsilon, r²+z²<=1}. D is a convex planar disk, so this is a solid torus with an explicit circle retraction from contracting D to an interior point. For each boundary-parallel upper arc, its supplied curtain disk gives a disjoint ball chart in which it is this straight arc. Cutting off those disjoint ball charts leaves a ball; reglue through disks to obtain the boundary connected sum of c standard solid tori. A finite central tree joined to the gluing disks is a contractible CW subcomplex of the remaining ball, hence its inclusion is a homotopy equivalence; the first clause of the same published CW lemma supplies the required relative SDR fixing the gluing disks. After contracting torus disk factors, the graph is a wedge of c circles.
upper_handlebody_local_model.still_to_write: The finite curtain-to-standard-ball charts and the central-ball assertion must be constructed explicitly from the disjoint planar arc strips. The solid-torus product calculation itself is complete, but it is not a substitute for those actual charts.

cap_product_neighborhood_realization.argument: Choose each footprint F as a convex polygonal disk and a lower convex cap C={(q,z):q∈F,h(q)<=z<=0}, with h piecewise linear, negative in intF and zero on ∂F. Choose two endpoint points p± in intF and a common interior vertex v of C. The V-shaped arc [p-,v] union [v,p+] is boundary-parallel in C, witnessed by its planar triangular disk to a top-face arc. Because C is convex, radial projection from v gives an explicit ball chart. A finite piecewise-linear sphere homeomorphism sending two antipodal boundary points to the radial directions of p±, extended radially, identifies this V-shaped core with a diameter core; choose endpoint disks as the images of the standard cylinder ends. Thus C is a product 0-handle around this chosen proper arc. Glue disjoint upper product tubes to these endpoint disks; the union has c 0-handles and c 1-handles in a single cycle and is a regular neighborhood of the normalized knot. Its lower exterior has exactly the terrain form of supplement2.
cap_product_neighborhood_realization.remaining_details: Must supply an actual finite triangulated boundary homeomorphism with endpoint disks and compatible collar coordinates, and smooth/round the PL core or explain transfer in the topological category to the supplied smooth normal tube. The proposed construction is explicit at the block level but not yet a complete written global proof. Do not certify on the word regular alone.
